steps.title: Import Angular core and create the main component
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and create the main component with selector 'app-root'
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component metadata including the selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main Angular component is created with the correct selector and empty template.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and the AppComponent class is decorated with @Component having selector 'app-root'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Component and created the main Angular component with the correct selector.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported Component from '@angular/core' and used the @Component decorator with selector 'app-root'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component setup isn't complete. You need to import Component from '@angular/core' and create a component class with the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Import Zustand and create the store interface
steps.instruction: Import the 'create' function from 'zustand' and define a TypeScript interface named 'CounterState' for the counter store state with a 'count' property of type number.
steps.hint: Add the import statement at the top of the file, then define the interface above the AppComponent class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the Zustand import and a CounterState interface defined.
successCriteria: The 'create' function is imported from 'zustand' and a 'CounterState' interface with a 'count: number' property is defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Zustand and defined the store interface with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've imported 'create' from 'zustand' and defined the CounterState interface with a 'count' property of type number.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import or interface definition is missing or incorrect. Check that you're importing 'create' from 'zustand' and defining a CounterState interface with 'count: number'.

steps.title: Create the basic Zustand store without persistence
steps.instruction: Create a basic counter store using Zustand's create() function with count state and increment/decrement actions. Define it as a constant named 'useCounterStore'.
steps.hint: Use Zustand's create function to define a store with initial state and actions. The store should have a count property and methods to increment and decrement it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zustand store named 'useCounterStore' is created with count state and increment/decrement actions.
successCriteria: The store is defined using create(), has a count property initialized to 0, and includes increment and decrement actions that update the count.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a basic Zustand store with count state and actions. This store will serve as the foundation before we add persistence.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your store includes both increment and decrement actions that properly update the count state using Zustand's set function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store definition is incomplete or incorrect. Remember to use Zustand's create() function with an initial state containing count: 0 and actions that update it.

steps.title: Import Zustand persist middleware
steps.instruction: Import the persist middleware from 'zustand/middleware' in your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Add an import statement for persist from the zustand middleware package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a middleware in Angular
import { persist } from 'zustand/middleware';
steps.expectedOutcome: The persist middleware is imported and available for use in your Zustand store.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the persist middleware, which will allow you to add persistence to your Zustand store.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing 'persist' specifically from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is incorrect. You need to import 'persist' from 'zustand/middleware'.

steps.title: Configure the persist middleware options
steps.instruction: Create a configuration object for the persist middleware with name and storage options. Define it as a constant named 'persistConfig'.
steps.hint: The persist middleware needs a configuration object specifying a name for the storage key and the storage mechanism to use.
steps.expectedOutcome: A persistConfig object is defined with name and storage properties.
successCriteria: The persistConfig object exists with 'name' and 'storage' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the persist configuration object with the required properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your persistConfig object includes both 'name' and 'storage' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The persist configuration object is missing or incomplete. It should have 'name' and 'storage' properties.

steps.title: Wrap the store with persist middleware
steps.instruction: Wrap your existing create() function call with the persist() middleware, passing your store configuration as the first argument and your persist configuration as the second argument.
steps.hint: The persist() function wraps the store creation function. It takes two arguments: the store creation function and the persist configuration object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store creation is now wrapped with the persist middleware, enabling automatic persistence of your state.
successCriteria: The persist() function is called with the store creation function and persist configuration as arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped your store with the persist middleware. This will automatically save and restore your state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling persist() with both arguments: the store creation function and the persist configuration object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The persist middleware isn't properly applied. Remember to wrap the create() function call with persist() and pass both required arguments.

steps.title: Initialize the store in the component
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent class, declare a property called 'store' and initialize it with the Zustand store you created earlier.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the class body, using the appropriate type for your store.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has access to the Zustand store through a class property.
successCriteria: store property is declared in AppComponent
store property is initialized with the Zustand store
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the Zustand store in your Angular component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've declared the store property, but make sure it's properly initialized with your Zustand store.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store property is missing or not properly initialized in the component class.

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent's @Component decorator, add a template property with a basic structure containing a container div and a heading element.
steps.hint: The template property should be a string containing HTML. Start with a div element and include an h1 inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic HTML structure in its template, ready for adding store-related UI elements.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a template property with a div containing an h1 element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the basic template structure. The div container and heading provide a foundation for displaying the store state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the template property contains both a div element and an h1 element inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't complete. Check that you've added a template property with a div containing an h1 element.

steps.title: Display the current count from store
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add a paragraph element that displays the current count value from the store using interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to interpolate the count value from the store property in your component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a value in Angular template

Current value: {{ myValue }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current count value from the store when rendered.
successCriteria: Template contains a paragraph element with interpolation that displays the count value from the store.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the current count from the store in the template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using interpolation with double curly braces to display the count value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the count value. Add a paragraph element with interpolation to show the count from the store.

steps.title: Add increment button and wire to store action
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a button element with the text 'Increment' and bind its click event to call the store's increment action.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="handler()" and call the increment method from your store instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with click handler
<button (click)="onIncrement()">Add One</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a button that, when clicked, will trigger the increment action from the Zustand store.
successCriteria: Click event is bound to store's increment action
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the increment button and wired it to the store action. The button will now increase the count when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a button with the correct text and the click event properly bound to call the store's increment method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or its click handler isn't set up correctly. Check that you have a button element with (click) event binding that calls the store's increment action.

steps.title: Add decrement button and wire to store action
steps.instruction: Add a decrement button to the template that calls the store's decrement action when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button element with a click event binding that calls the store's decrement method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a decrement button that will decrease the count when clicked.
successCriteria: A decrement button is added to the template with a click event binding to store.decrement()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a decrement button that calls the store's decrement action.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct click event binding to store.decrement().
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement button is missing or not properly wired to the store's decrement action.

steps.title: Test persistence by refreshing the page
steps.instruction: Add a decrement button to the template next to the increment button, then test persistence by incrementing/decrementing and refreshing the browser to verify the count is restored.
steps.hint: Add a button element with a click handler that calls store.decrement(). After adding it, interact with both buttons and refresh the page to see if the count persists.
steps.expectedOutcome: A decrement button appears next to the increment button, and after interacting with both buttons and refreshing the browser, the count value persists.
successCriteria: The template includes a decrement button wired to store.decrement(), and persistence is verified by refreshing the page.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the decrement button and verified that the Zustand persist middleware works correctly—the count persists across page refreshes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the decrement button, but did you test persistence by refreshing the page? Try incrementing/decrementing, then refresh to see if the count is restored.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement button is missing or not properly wired. Make sure to add a button with (click)="store.decrement()" and test persistence by refreshing the browser.
